title: Everything Depends on Your Hammer: A Systematic Rowhammer Attack Exploration on SPHINCS+
problem: Post-quantum cryptographic implementations are vulnerable to rowhammer-based fault injection attacks on native systems, where remote attackers can forge digital signatures.
motivation: As quantum computing advances, securing PQC implementations against practical fault attacks is critical for cloud and multi-user systems.
method: Characterize the DRAM fault model on specific platforms (DDR3/DDR4), then devise optimal rowhammer attacks by analyzing fault patterns. Demonstrate a forgery attack on SPHINCS+ using rowhammer on standard liboqs implementation.
key_novelty: First rowhammer-based forgery attack on SPHINCS+ (NIST standard), demonstrating practical fault injection threats for hash-based digital signatures in cloud systems.
contributions: System-specific fault characterization approach for native systems vs. embedded systems
Novel rowhammer-based forgery attack on SPHINCS+ with DDR3/DDR4 DRAM
Practical demonstration on standard liboqs library implementation
Platform-optimized attack methodology exploiting target-specific fault susceptibility

metrics.other: demonstrated on DDR3 and DDR4 DRAM

limitations: Attack requires direct process access on target system; effectiveness depends on target DRAM susceptibility to rowhammer.
